name: Dug wells in Neolithic Cyprus
summary: At Kissonerga-Mylouthkia, charred cereal remains from the fill of Well 116 indicate that it had been dug by about 8200 cal BCE.
description: Kissonerga-Mylouthkia has pre-pottery Neolithic wells. Well 116 belongs to Period 1A. The excavator dates short-lived cereal remains from its fill to roughly 8600–8200 cal BCE. Two dated seeds from the later Well 133 give a calibrated range of 7500–6700 cal BCE as reported in the palaeogenomic study. These finds date material in the fills and provide approximate latest bounds for the digging of the wells.

impact.note: Scored as the well-digging of one island's early farming communities (reach 1), though the source opened documents a single well; a water supply independent of streams and springs was a new capability (depth 2); no later well tradition is shown to descend from the Cypriot wells (generativity 0).

date.label: Approximately 8600–8200 cal BCE (Well 116 fill samples)
date.basis: The excavator’s synthesis of three short-lived cereal samples from fills 123 and 124, table 11.1; this dates material from the fill.

events.statement: Three charred cereal samples from two fills of Well 116 at Kissonerga-Mylouthkia date to roughly 8600–8200 cal BCE in the excavator’s synthesis.

evidence.supports: The final report records sample provenance and age estimates. Well 116 existed before those fills accumulated.

date.label: 7500-6700 cal BCE (fill of well 133)
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Two carbonised seeds from one fill of well 133 at Kissonerga-Mylouthkia give a calibrated range of 7500 to 6700 BCE at 95% confidence; this dates the filling, so the well had been dug by then.

evidence.supports: The calibrated date range of these samples is 7500–6700 cal BCE
evidence.locator: Methods, archaeological context of the samples from well 133

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest documented dated fill for this local record, preceding the dated fill of Well 133.

unresolved.note: The excavator compares contemporary Shillourokambos features and later Atlit-Yam and North Mesopotamian wells. Reassess those individual features before claiming priority, transmission or descent.
The date is from seeds in a fill, which gives a latest date for the digging of the well, not the date of digging.
Kissonerga coordinates were entered from memory and not taken from a fetched source.
The author list should be checked against the journal page.

research.note: The two wells have separately documented fills. The final excavation report gives older evidence at Well 116. The record’s date claims refer to the sampled contexts; the origin and diffusion of the technique remain open.
